expectations_gap.basis: Reverse DCF solves a NEGATIVE 6.49% five-year implied FCF CAGR against an achieved three-year revenue CAGR of 15.12%, the opposite direction from Caterpillar/Cummins above: the market is pricing continued cash-flow decline while revenue has been growing double digits. The roughly 22-point gap exceeds the 3.59-point horizon_spread. This could read as a cheap-entry expectations gap or as the market correctly discounting the near-zero net income and elevated leverage flagged in quality; recorded plainly as a real, measured gap without adjudicating which explanation holds, which is Stocky's question.
